name: reviewbot-runner-failure-answers-trigger
description:
A triggered review that the RUNNER fails before the agent answers the pull request must still leave the pull request answered.

A signed pull_request webhook spawns the session, the agent claims the check run (it now reads in progress), and then the session runs out of budget: the fixture class allows two model turns, so the runner fails the session itself (BudgetExceeded) at the top of the third, before the agent ever reaches conclude_trigger_status. The runner does not answer the trigger; the operator does, from its backstop for every Failed session whose trigger is still open. Before that backstop existed only the operator's own failure paths (a boot failure, the maxDuration backstop) answered a trigger, so a failure the runner wrote — a budget cap, a halt, a provider error that outlasted its retries — left the check run showing the work in progress for good.

The assertions are on the CHECK RUN, not on anything the agent said: it is completed, concluded neutral (could_not_finish's github mapping — a review that could not run is not a verdict on the change), its summary is the framework's 'stopped before it finished' text carrying the failure reason token, and it is the SAME run the claim opened (one create, one update), not a second run stacked on the commit. The counts pin only that: the run was closed once, on the run the claim opened. They do NOT show that a later backstop pass stays off the provider, because a pass that re-read an already-concluded run would write nothing either and leave the same counts; that the TriggerAnswered marker stops later passes is pinned by the operator's unit tests (failedtrigger_test.go). The session phase barrier pins that the session really ended Failed rather than idling.
